```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = FALSE, collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

Use Azure SQL in a Shiny app while keeping access to the data under your
database's existing permissions. Visitors sign in with their Microsoft
account, and Azure SQL decides which tables and rows they can query.

Azure SQL is Microsoft's hosted SQL database; SQL Server can also run on
your own infrastructure. `oauth_db_azure_sql()` gives your app a DBI
connection for SQL or dbplyr queries. The first example lists the tables
the signed-in user can access.

## Try the guided demo

Run `shinyOAuthDB::oauth_db_cloud_demo("azure-sql")` in the R console to
set up an editable local app. It asks for your database and Microsoft app
registration, and explains where to find each setting. You can save a draft
while an administrator arranges access.

The demo needs `odbc`, `bslib`, `processx`, `askpass` and Microsoft ODBC
Driver 18. Sign in, then click **Run example query** to connect. Stopping
the local app leaves the Azure database running. See
[Getting started](getting-started.html#more-ways-to-try-an-app) for editing
and `?oauth_db_cloud_demo` for the launcher arguments.

## Set up access

Install
[Microsoft ODBC Driver 18](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/connect/odbc/download-odbc-driver-for-sql-server)
for your operating system. Your database
administrator must [enable Microsoft Entra authentication](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-sql/database/authentication-aad-configure?view=azuresql)
and give users or their groups access to the database.

Create a Microsoft Entra Web app registration with permission to access
SQL on a user's behalf. Register `http://localhost:8100` as its redirect
URI, then save these values in a local `.Renviron` file and restart R:

```text
OAUTHDB_TENANT_ID=your-tenant-id
OAUTHDB_CLIENT_ID=your-client-id
OAUTHDB_CLIENT_SECRET=your-client-secret
```

Follow [Microsoft app registration](#register-a-microsoft-entra-app)
to find the IDs and secret. Add the **Azure SQL Database** delegated
`user_impersonation` permission and obtain consent as your tenant requires.

| Value in the app | Where to find it |
| --- | --- |
| `server` | Azure portal: SQL database overview, **Server name** |
| `database` | The database's name in Azure, not the logical server name |
| Tenant ID and client ID | Entra app registration overview |
| Client secret | Registration's **Certificates & secrets**, secret **Value** |

In Azure, allow the app server's IP or private network to reach SQL.
Creating an app registration doesn't open the database firewall.

### Register a Microsoft Entra app

In the [Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com/), open
**App registrations** and create a registration in your organization's
tenant. Copy **Application (client) ID** and **Directory (tenant) ID**
from its overview. Under **Authentication**, add a **Web** platform with
`http://localhost:8100` as the redirect URI. Under **Certificates & secrets**,
create a client secret and copy its **Value** before leaving.
Microsoft's [registration instructions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity-platform/quickstart-register-app)
describe the available account types.

Under **API permissions**, add the delegated permission for your data
source: **Azure SQL Database** uses `user_impersonation`. Azure PostgreSQL
uses **Azure OSSRDBMS Database** access; Fabric API permissions depend on
the operations in the [Fabric guide](fabric.html). An administrator may
need to grant consent or allow the application. The database administrator
must separately give the user or their group database access.

## A complete app

Save this as `example.R`, replacing the server and database:

After signing in,
click **Load rows**. The app starts its workers once and stops them at shutdown.

```{r app}
library(shiny)
library(shinyOAuth)
library(shinyOAuthDB)

client <- oauth_db_microsoft_client(
  services = "sql",
  tenant_id = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_TENANT_ID"),
  client_id = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_CLIENT_ID"),
  client_secret = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_CLIENT_SECRET"),
  redirect_uri = "http://localhost:8100"
)

ui <- oauth_ui(
  fluidPage(
    actionButton("login", "Sign in"),
    actionButton("logout", "Sign out"),

    actionButton("load", "Load rows"),
    tableOutput("rows")
  ),

  id = "auth",
  client = client
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  auth <- oauth_module_server(
    "auth",
    client,
    auto_redirect = FALSE,
    async = TRUE
  )

  observeEvent(input$login, auth$request_login())
  observeEvent(input$logout, auth$logout())

  con <- oauth_db_azure_sql(
    auth$connection,
    server = "example.database.windows.net",
    database = "Reporting"
  )

  query_task <- oauth_db_task(con)

  observeEvent(input$load, {
    query_task$invoke("SELECT TOP (20) name FROM sys.tables")
  })

  output$rows <- renderTable(query_task$result())
}

runApp(
  shinyApp(ui, server, uiPattern = ".*", onStart = function() {
    mirai::daemons(2)

    onStop(function() mirai::daemons(0))
  }),
  port = 8100,
  launch.browser = FALSE
)

# Open the app in your regular browser at its registered redirect URI.
```

Run `source("example.R")` and open
`http://localhost:8100`. Sign in to run the query; signing out clears the
output.

## Query with dbplyr

In the app, `con` is a function. The task opens the signed-in user's DBI connection in its worker.

To read an `Orders` table with dbplyr, install `dbplyr` and `dplyr`,
then replace the output expression with:

```{r dbplyr-query}
fetch_rows <- function(connection) {
  dplyr::tbl(connection, "Orders") |>
    dplyr::filter(amount > 100) |>
    dplyr::collect()
}

query_task <- oauth_db_task(con, method = fetch_rows)

observeEvent(input$load, query_task$invoke())

output$rows <- renderTable(query_task$result())
```

For SQL queries that include values entered by a user, use DBI parameter
binding.

## Give users database access

An administrator first sets an Entra administrator on the Azure SQL logical
server. Connect to the target database with that administrator and create
an external user or group, then grant the intended access. For example:

```sql
CREATE USER [reporting-readers] FROM EXTERNAL PROVIDER;
GRANT SELECT ON OBJECT::dbo.Orders TO [reporting-readers];
```

Use an existing Entra group name and your actual table. This establishes
database permissions for its members; OAuth registration alone doesn't.
Microsoft's [Entra configuration guide](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-sql/database/authentication-aad-configure?view=azuresql)
covers administrator setup and external users.

## Other SQL Server deployments

Use the same `oauth_db_azure_sql()` helper for SQL Managed Instance or
Synapse SQL, with that deployment's server and database. For SQL Server
configured to accept Entra tokens, use `oauth_db_sql_server()` with the
same arguments and client.

See `?oauth_db_azure_sql` for driver settings such as `driver`, `port`,
and `timeout`. [Getting started](getting-started.html#sessions-saved-results-and-extra-permissions) covers
custom permissions and existing logins.
